question: What is the primary focus of health economics in the healthcare sector?

options.A: Minimizing clinical staff to reduce hospital overhead
options.B: Maximizing pharmaceutical sales across public hospitals
options.C: Allocating scarce resources to maximize health outcomes
options.D: Eliminating all out-of-pocket expenses for patients

explanation: Health economics centers on how limited resources are distributed to achieve the best possible health benefits for populations. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why has nursing care traditionally been viewed as an invisible component of hospital charges?

options.A: Patients directly pay nurses hourly wages at the bedside
options.B: Nursing tasks are entirely administrative rather than clinical
options.C: It was bundled into general room rates rather than itemized
options.D: Hospitals legally prohibited nurses from generating revenue

explanation: Grouping nursing care into the general cost of a hospital bed masks the specific financial value and labor intensity of professional nursing services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: What does the process of costing nursing services primarily involve?

options.A: Setting monthly salary scales for administrative hospital directors
options.B: Determining the market price of medical diagnostic equipment
options.C: Calculating the yearly profit margins of private pharmacies
options.D: Identifying and measuring resources consumed during care delivery

explanation: Costing calculates the specific financial inputs, including labor and materials, required to provide nursing care to patients. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: How does accurate costing of nursing labor help nurse managers during budget cuts?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for hospital financial audits
options.B: It allows the hospital to replace all professional nurses with volunteers
options.C: It guarantees an automatic increase in government tax subventions
options.D: It justifies required staffing levels by demonstrating financial value

explanation: Data on the precise economic cost of care prevents arbitrary downsizing by proving that nursing personnel are essential revenue and clinical assets. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following represents a direct cost in nursing care?

options.A: Administrative wages of the central human resources office
options.B: Monthly electricity bill for the entire hospital complex
options.C: Salary of the bedside nurse administering intravenous fluids
options.D: Depreciation value of the main hospital administrative building

explanation: Direct costs are expenses directly tied to the care of a specific patient, such as the hands-on labor of the bedside nurse. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why are ward lighting and laundry services classified as indirect costs?

options.A: They represent expenses that occur entirely outside the hospital grounds
options.B: They fluctuate daily based on the exact diagnosis of each admission
options.C: They support overall facility operations rather than one specific patient
options.D: They are billed directly to the patient's personal insurance policy

explanation: Indirect costs are shared overhead expenses that cannot be traced to a single individual patient encounter. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: What defines a fixed cost in a clinical setting?

options.A: A fee that increases every time a patient receives an injection
options.B: Daily wages paid exclusively to temporary registry nurses
options.C: The fluctuating cost of buying emergency surgical supplies
options.D: An expense that remains constant regardless of patient volume

explanation: Fixed costs do not change when patient census rises or falls, remaining stable over the short term. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: A sudden surge in ward admissions leads to a sharp increase in the consumption of disposable syringes. How is this expense classified?
explanation: Variable costs fluctuate directly with patient volume and clinical activity, rising as more patients require hands-on supplies. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary characteristic of the micro-costing approach in healthcare finance?

options.A: It tracks every single resource and minute of care for an individual patient
options.B: It estimates departmental overhead without evaluating bedside nursing tasks
options.C: It calculates expenses based solely on the total number of hospital beds
options.D: It relies exclusively on high-level, aggregate hospital budget summaries

explanation: Micro-costing provides high-detail data by examining every specific item and minute of labor consumed by a specific patient. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which costing methodology maps the exact clinical pathway and calculates the cost of capacity per unit of time?
explanation: Time-driven activity-based costing evaluates the time and capacity required to perform specific care processes along a clinical pathway. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Patient Classification System in nursing administration?

options.A: To determine the architectural layout of hospital wards
options.B: To assess the maintenance schedule of heavy diagnostic machinery
options.C: To categorize patients based on dependency and clinical complexity
options.D: To calculate the annual tax liability of private healthcare facilities

explanation: Patient classification systems group individuals by their care needs and dependency levels to measure workload accurately. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why must nursing costing models incorporate patient acuity data from classification systems?

options.A: Hospital accreditation boards prohibit charging flat rates for bed occupancy
options.B: Insurers refuse to pay for any patient admitted with a surgical diagnosis
options.C: Acuity scores automatically determine the pharmaceutical budget for the state
options.D: Complex patients require more intensive nursing hours and higher resource costs

explanation: Acuity-based costing reflects the reality that caring for unstable, dependent patients demands significantly more nursing time and financial resources. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is a major barrier to accurate nursing costing in many Nigerian public health facilities?

options.A: Strict government mandates requiring micro-costing in all primary clinics
options.B: Excessive availability of fully automated electronic health record software
options.C: Reliance on paper-based record systems that hinder granular data tracking
options.D: Complete absence of any nursing personnel within tertiary hospitals

explanation: Manual paper documentation makes it extremely difficult to capture detailed, time-stamped records of nursing tasks for cost analysis. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: How do out-of-pocket payment models complicate standardized tariff setting for nursing services?

options.A: They create unpredictable billing streams that bypass centralized insurance structures
options.B: They eliminate the need to calculate direct and indirect operational costs
options.C: They guarantee fixed monthly government subventions for every registered nurse
options.D: They standardize all hospital purchases across the entire country

explanation: When patients pay individually for disparate items on a cash basis, establishing uniform, predictable pricing models for nursing care becomes highly complex. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is a primary benefit of financial literacy for nurse managers?

options.A: It removes all clinical responsibilities from their daily work schedules
options.B: It completely replaces the need for hospital financial officers
options.C: It allows them to personally audit the personal finances of patients
options.D: It empowers them to negotiate effectively for adequate staffing and resources

explanation: Financial literacy gives nurse managers the economic data and language needed to advocate successfully for their units at executive levels. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)

question: Which outcome is most likely when nurse managers successfully utilize transparent costing data during budget reviews?

options.A: Hospital administrators immediately eliminate all indirect operational expenses
options.B: Nursing staff is recognized as a vital clinical investment rather than disposable overhead
options.C: The facility transitions exclusively to a volunteer-based nursing workforce
options.D: Government funding agencies reduce subventions due to increased efficiency

explanation: Demonstrating the exact economic value of nursing care reframes staffing as an essential driver of safety and quality rather than a mere cost burden. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)
